Gd(3+)/Ca(2+) entry in pancreatic acinar cell is targeted to mitochondria and that mitochondria are involved in the control of exocytotic secretion in these cells.

mitochondrial Ca(2+) accumulation, via capacitative Ca( 2+) entry, regulates both the amplitude and the duration of the Ca( 2+ ) response to agonist stimulation and that this is instrumental in governing the mode of exocytotic secretion.
capacitative Ca(3+) entry, which is targeted directly to the lateral plasma membrane, is instrumental in shaping exocytotic responses in rat pancreatic acini.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how mitochondria shape the exocytosis response of rat pancreatic cells.
the role of mitochondria in regulating the exocytosis of secretory vesicles in pancreatic acinar cell.
the role of mitochondria in regulating secretory activity in rat pancreatic acini.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in rat pancreatic cells, capacitative store-mediated entry is not a major pathway of Ca(2+), but is a major pathway for the release of mitochondrial messengers that regulate exocytosis.
mitochondrial Ca(2+) is the key factor in determining the secretory response of rat pancreatic exocrine cells.
mitochondria are a critical regulator of exocytotic activity in rat pancreatic acini.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in rat pancreatic cells, Ca(2+), released from intracellular stores, activates capacitative Ca( 2+) entry which is targeted to mitochondria.
in rat pancreatic cells the Ca(2+) store is the primary source of Ca(2+), which is released in two distinct phases.

in rat pancreatic cells, Ca(2+) is the primary messenger, and the Ca(2+)+/Ca(2+) pump and Ca(2+)/calmodulin kinase II are the primary effectors, but Ca(2+) can be "fine-tuned" by a number of second and third messenger systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial function plays a critical role in determining the exocytosis mode of rat pancreatic acini.
mitochondria are not simply a sink for Ca(2+).
the mitochondrial Ca(+)2 store is a major player in the control of the exocytosis in rat pancreatic acini, and it is a major target for Gd(+)3.
